thread:
noah: Quick debrief from last week's guerilla testing on the Credentials page. Two consistent pain points: people can't quickly see "what this key can actually do" and they're nervous about the finality of Revoke.

tara: Good summary. What concrete tweaks did we test that landed?

noah: We tried three small changes: 1) 'Policy preview' panel showing a one-line human summary + a collapsed code snippet of concrete curl examples. 2) Soft-revoke option (UI marks it revoked, tokens stay live for a short grace period with countdown). 3) Sticky copy CTA on mobile for rotated secrets.

ben: On the policy preview, folks liked seeing sample requests. Example we showed: `curl -X POST /v1/embeddings` -> 200, `curl -X POST /v1/generate` -> 403. It made scopes less abstract.

izzy: Accessibility note: when policy preview changes (user toggles a scope), announce the new one-line summary via aria-live and make the sample requests reachable by keyboard.

noah: Revoke language: users reacted poorly to unilateral "Revoke". We prototyped a 2-step label: primary button "Mark revoked (grace: 10m)" + a danger menu item "Force revoke now". People felt less panicked.

tara: Implementation question: where is that 10m coming from? org default or per-key?

noah: Proposal: org default editable by admins; per-key override shown inline as a small link "This key uses org default (10m) — change". If you change org default, show a lightweight modal explaining system-wide effects.

ben: For rotation, testers expected an explicit checklist after generating a secret: "1) Copy secret (only shown once) 2) Update CI 3) Restart running jobs". We surfaced that as three small checkboxes with a prominent copy button.

izzy: On the secret reveal, keyboard flow matters: set focus to the Copy button, add an aria-live polite announcement: "API key revealed. Press Copy to copy to clipboard. This key will not be shown again." Avoid assertive since it can interrupt screen readers.

noah: Mobile UX: when secret is visible, show a sticky bottom bar with Copy + Dismiss. Users rarely scrolled down to the revealed area.

tara: Any thoughts on defaults for audit logging and telemetry?

ben: We recommend: default audit logging ON for admins, OFF for regular users, but show a contextual microcopy: "Admins: rotation & revoke events will be recorded to audit logs." Also expose a per-key toggle in the modal.

izzy: Tiny copy nit for broad scopes: prefer concrete phrasing: "This key may create tokens and generate completions. Consider restricting to a service account or using an embeddings-only preset." Add a link to mitigations.

noah: Also prototyped ephemeral permission presets: small pills like Embeddings, Read-only, Full. Clicking a pill expands a short inline summary — users liked that better than a dense table.

access-bot: Reminder: please attach the annotated a11y checklist and the Figma frames to the #design-review thread before EOD.

noah: Will do. I'll upload the frames with the accessible focus notes and the curl snippets. Thanks all! :pray:
